source.title: Different Corruptions, Different Signals: Uncertainty and Loss in Federated Data Quality
source.authors: Bradley Scott; Zeqi Luo; Edmond S. L. Ho

page_placements.theme: Identifying corrupted supervision depends on the diagnostic and training conditions

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text includes the paper and appendix tables.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests corruption-detection signals in federated learning, not whether networks fit random labels or how training error changes. Its results do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The study measures whether uncertainty and prediction-label loss distinguish corrupted from clean samples. Its discussion that sufficiently long training may fit corrupted labels cites prior work, so it is not recorded as a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures corruption-detection AUC on local validation probes, not training-set memorization, convergence time, or learning order. Section III-C cites Arpit et al. for the possibility of fitting corrupted labels with longer training. Declining clean-test accuracy under increasing label corruption does not establish V4's accompanying perfect training fit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: prediction-label loss detects persistent random flips while input-conditional uncertainty remains at chance; expected entropy modestly outperforms loss for additive image noise, with its advantage becoming apparent as federation-wide corruption prevalence increases.
record.recipe_differences: Federated ResNet-20 training with FedAvg and uncertainty-aware loss attenuation; measures corruption-detection AUC rather than random-label training fit.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and corruption type; for image noise, expected-entropy advantage over loss becomes apparent as federation-wide corruption prevalence increases. Per-client rankings vary substantially with Dirichlet partitioning.

fits_no_version.finding: For persistent random flips, within-client validation-probe uncertainty AUC is 0.49–0.50, while prediction-label loss AUC is 0.85 on CIFAR-10 and 0.95 on SVHN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this federated ResNet-20 setup, prediction-label loss detects persistent random label flips better than the evaluated input-conditional uncertainty scores.

fits_no_version.finding: For additive image noise, expected-entropy AUC is 0.67/0.66 versus loss AUC 0.64/0.64; aleatoric variance is weak on CIFAR-10 and inverted on SVHN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Corruption-detection performance depends on corruption type and uncertainty estimator; expected entropy modestly outperforms loss for the tested image noise.

record.problems: The study evaluates one architecture, two datasets, one Gaussian-noise level, and persistent random flips; authors state that class-consistent flips, other architectures, datasets, client counts, local objectives, aggregation strategies, and corruption models remain to be tested. The within-client results may retain residual differences in class composition or intrinsic sample difficulty. The cause of inverted AV on SVHN noise is unresolved.
record.rows_left_out: Per-client detection AUCs (Tables I, V, VI), clean-data control AUCs (Section IV-B), and clean-test accuracy by M and q (Table III) were omitted because they concern client ranking or downstream accuracy, not a listed claim version. The full M × q grids for within-client detection (Table IV) were omitted because the requested claim versions do not test detection performance.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true and random labels, and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep and the joint progression of test error toward chance. Table III reports only clean-test accuracy over a restricted corruption range.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Temporal evidence that shared real-data patterns are fitted before noisy labels are memorized.

record.verdict_notes: All Table II values and chance baselines match the text. The original row states describe detection performance, so they cannot serve as states for V1–V6. The probes are validation splits, and AUC measures relative ranking rather than absolute fit. Lower flip-detection loss AUC at higher corruption prevalence does not demonstrate memorization or its timing.

versions.untested_parts: Training error on completely random labels, test error at chance, and whether the original architecture and hyperparameters suffice.
Relative training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Training on shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training-set fit across corruption rates and the corresponding test-error trend.
Whether regularization prevents random-label fitting or its removal harms true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

relation.reason: Section III-C cites Arpit et al. for the possibility that sufficiently long training fits individual corrupted labels; the study neither tests nor uses that finding as a tool.

tranche.reason: The study measures corruption-detection AUC on validation probes and clean-test accuracy. It does not measure training-set fitting, fitting time, temporal learning order, or the other claim-version effects.

source_check.notes: Table II reports grid-averaged validation-probe detection AUCs using rounds 41–50. Chance-level uncertainty detection and strong loss detection establish neither the presence nor absence of random-label training fit.
